Subject: Sizing ask — isolation requirement for pilot (HIPAA)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a small pilot (3 months) that handles PHI and our security team is asking for a clear capacity proposal comparing: (A) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, shared control plane) vs (B) Redwood Private (VPC + customer-managed control plane / air-gapped variant).

Key constraints from security: no cross-tenant KV cache sharing, tenancy isolation, separate logging/audit retention, and ability to bring our own KMS. For procurement: we need an estimate for a short-term pilot (# GPUs, expected RPS, monthly run-rate) and a clear migration path to production if pilot is successful.

Can you share a compact comparison and a recommended starting footprint for the pilot? Also let me know what artifacts (SOC2 evidence, network diagram) you need from our side.

—Alex
Alex Murray
Director, AI Integrations 
ClearWay Health
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing ask — isolation requirement for pilot (HIPAA)

Alex — thanks for the clear requirements. I attached a short MPA checklist (clearway_mpa_requirements.pdf) and an isolation sizing workbook with two starter slates. High-level summary below — I put conservative numbers for pilot headroom and a migration ladder to avoid rework later.

Quick recommendation (pilot, 3 months):
- Dedicated (reserved) pilot slate: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared control plane, tenant isolation via dedicated pools). Good if you want faster ramp and lower onboarding friction.
- Private (VPC/on-prem equivalent) pilot slate: 3 x A100-equivalent GPUs behind customer VPC + private control plane. Slightly higher per-GPU cost, more lead time for network setup, but strongest isolation and KMS-on-customer-side fit.

Estimated pilot throughput (tokenized workload, mixed chat/generation): 300–500 concurrent sessions peak => expect ~18–25 RPS of generation requests depending on prompt lengths. We model for 20 RPS sustained with bursts to 40. Workbook shows queueing latency at those points.

Migration ladder: start with Dedicated (fastest) and switch to Private after security sign-off if you want to move to customer-managed KMS + audit pipeline. If you need absolute custody from day 1, choose Private — we estimate 2–3 week longer onboarding window.

Attachments: isolation_sizing_workbook.xlsx (detailed token/latency model), cost-model-dedicated_vs_private.csv

Next steps: if this aligns, Marissa will send a pilot commercial term (3-month reserved vs month-to-month private). Karthik will add a short ops checklist for the networking/KMS handover.

Thanks,
—Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: isolation sizing — ops and kernel/quant recommendations

Alex / Kimberly / Marissa — a few technical clarifications to set accurate sizing in the workbook:

1) Model family and sequence length assumption: we assumed a 4k-context LLM with average response length ~180 tokens. If you're planning for longer-context (8k+), increase GPU slate by ~50% or use a lower quantized model with slightly higher latency.

2) KV cache isolation: Dedicated mode can enforce per-tenant cache isolation within the serving runtime; Private mode has the same isolation but also isolates control plane telemetry to your VPC. From an ops perspective, both meet "no cross-tenant KV leakage" but Private provides stronger evidence for auditors (network separation + KMS you control).

3) Batching & latency: we recommend enabling small-window continuous batching and prefix KV caching. Workbook simulates a 30ms batching window which gives ~2.3x cost efficiency at the target mix.

4) Infrastructure sizing summary (pilot):
- Dedicated: 4 x A100-e, 256GB GPU RAM effective (model sharding/tiling applied), 1.5TB NVMe cache across nodes, autoscale headroom for +50% bursts.
- Private: 3 x A100-e, 512GB aggregated cache (customer-managed NVMe), prioritized network egress routes for logs/audit.

If you want, I can run a second workbook scenario assuming an 8k-long context model and return the revised GPU counts by EOD.

—Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Inference Platforms
